facts.statement: The only known specimen was found at Cerro Cóndor Sur, about a kilometer west of the village of Cerro Cóndor in Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Volkheimeria was discovered at the site of Cerro Cóndor Sur, roughly a kilometer west of the village of Cerro Cóndor in Chubut Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: José Bonaparte described Volkheimeria chubutensis as a new genus and species in 1979.
facts.quote: In 1979, José Bonaparte described it as representing a new genus and species, Volkheimeria chubutensis, alongside two other species discovered in the same strata, Piatnitzkysaurus floresi and Patagosaurus fariasi.

facts.statement: The genus name Volkheimeria honors the Argentine paleontologist Wolfgang Volkheimer.
facts.quote: The genus name Volkheimeria honors the Argentinean paleontologist Wolfgang Volkheimer.

facts.statement: Only one specimen, the holotype PVL 4077, is known from the Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Only a single specimen of Volkheimeria chubutensis is known: the holotype PVL 4077, a partial skeleton from the Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of partial cervical and dorsal vertebrae, part of the sacrum, incomplete tail vertebrae, partial pelvic bones, and hind limb bones including a femur and tibia.
facts.quote: This specimen consists of a partial cervical vertebra, two complete and two partial dorsal vertebrae, part of the sacrum, several incomplete caudal vertebrae, partial ilia, a pubis, an ischium, a femur, and a tibia.

facts.statement: The size of a fully grown Volkheimeria is unknown because the known specimen is immature.
facts.quote: The size of a fully-grown Volkheimeria is not known, as it is only known from an immature specimen.

facts.statement: A potentially associated tooth is broad and spoon-shaped with large denticles on the upper two-thirds of the crown.
facts.quote: A tooth that may belong to Volkheimeria is broad and spoon-shaped, with large denticles present on the upper two-thirds of the tooth crown.

facts.statement: Pleurocoels, air sac cavities in the vertebrae, are present in the cervical vertebrae but absent in the dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Pleurocoels, excavations in the side of the vertebrae for air sacs, were present in the cervical vertebrae but not the dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The tibia is relatively short compared to the femur, measuring only 58% of its length.
facts.quote: The tibia is fairly short relative to the femur, at only 58% of its length.

facts.statement: Volkheimeria is considered a relatively small species with an estimated length of 10 to 12 meters.
facts.quote: Volkheimeria es una especie bastante pequeña con una longitud estimada de 10 a 12 metros.

facts.statement: The ilium has a length of 45 centimeters.
facts.quote: El ilion tiene una longitud de 45 centímetros.

facts.statement: The femur lacks a lesser trochanter and is 70% longer than the tibia.
facts.quote: El fémur no tiene trocánter menor y es un 70% más largo que la tibia.

facts.statement: A 2017 histological examination of the femur indicated rapid growth with no clear growth rings.
facts.quote: El examen histológico del fémur en 2017 indicó un crecimiento rápido, sin anillos de crecimiento claros.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses have variably recovered Volkheimeria as a eusauropod, vulcanodontid, or primitive sauropod due to its incomplete nature.
facts.quote: Some phylogenetic analyses of the taxon have recovered it as a eusauropod, vulcanodontid, or primitive sauropod, though its position is variable due to its incomplete nature.

facts.statement: Originally identified as a possible cetiosaurid and later a brachiosaurid, Volkheimeria is now considered a eusauropod, specifically a relatively primitive one compared to Patagosaurus.
facts.quote: Originalmente identificado como un posible cetiosáurido junto con Patagosaurus y luego identificado como braquiosáurido por un tiempo, Volkheimeria ahora se considera un eusaurópodo junto con Patagosaurus y Lapparentosaurus, con Volkheimeria y Lapparentosaurus, eusaurópodos relativamente primitivos en comparación con el Patagosaurus más derivado.

facts.statement: Volkheimeria lived during the Toarcian age of the Early Jurassic, 178 to 179 million years ago.
facts.quote: Volkheimeria lived during the Toarcian age of the Early Jurassic, 178-179 million years ago.
